_comment: Adjudication of the rewording screen from scripts/verify-new-ideas.ts. Each title here is a separate agent's version of an idea another agent (or the board) already covers, so it is not imported. Decisions are recorded with the reason, because the screen itself is a net and cannot tell a duplicate from a shared-vocabulary coincidence. Titles match on normalised form (lowercase, punctuation collapsed).

reviewed.pair: Zero-result search gap report (badge) vs Zero-result search to gap briefs (content)
reviewed.reason: Same insight and same input (mine no-result searches for catalogue gaps). The content version is the superset: it clusters the queries into themes and produces both editorial briefs and alias/synonym work, whereas the badge version only triages single rows.

reviewed.pair: Per-Game Mastery Unlocks (game) vs Per-game mastery tracks (addon) vs Per-Game Mastery Tracks (xp)
reviewed.decision: drop the game and xp versions, keep the addon one
reviewed.reason: Three agents independently produced per-game mastery scored from that game's rounds. The addon version is the most complete (the scoring formula with recency weighting, named tiers, and how it is displayed); the other two are the same system with one facet emphasised. The xp-scope copy is dropped by the importer's title dedup, since its normalised title is identical to the survivor's. Worth folding in when it is built: the game-scope variant's rule that unlocks are gameplay modifiers rather than currency.

reviewed.pair: Cross-Game Variety Streak (game) vs Cross-game handoff streak (addon)
reviewed.reason: Same incentive (reward playing a different game than last time) with the same chain-and-reset shape. The addon version specifies how the bonus grows through distinct games and when the chain resets, so it is the one to keep. Worth folding in: the game variant's concrete enforcement rule (the server keeps the member's last five game ids).

reviewed.pair: Counter-heist revenge window (addon) vs Revenge Counter-Steal Window (coin)
reviewed.reason: The same mechanic: a member who was robbed gets one boosted counter-attempt against that specific thief inside a short window, single-use so it cannot become a farm. Only the window length differs (24 h vs 1 h) and whether the attempt is free or discounted, which are parameters of one idea, not two ideas.

reviewed.pair: Training-wheels loss rebate (addon) vs Session Loss Rebate (coin)
reviewed.reason: Both are a loss rebate: coins returned after losing rounds. The audience and trigger differ (new accounts below level 5 vs a losing session for everyone), but the idea is the same one parameterised twice. Worth folding in: the level-5 expiry that makes the new-player version self-limiting.

reviewed.pair: Wanted board with restitution (addon) vs Steal Bounty Board (coin)
reviewed.reason: The same mechanic: a robbed member posts a bounty on the thief, claimed by successfully stealing from that thief, verified from steal_attempts, forfeited if unclaimed inside a window. Found by a pairwise body-similarity scan over all 444 imported ideas, not by the title screen (their titles share almost nothing, and their bodies scored 0.51 — just under the screen's 0.60 threshold, which is why the extra pass was worth running). Worth folding in: the addon variant's rolling 'most wanted' ranking and its aggregation floor, which keeps small heists out of a public shaming list.

kept_after_review.pair: Steal Bounty Board (coin) vs Data-Quality Bounty Board (game)
kept_after_review.reason: Share only the words 'bounty board'. One is a bounty on stealing coins, the other on reporting catalogue data problems.

kept_after_review.pair: Community tags on badges (badge) vs Community museum of extinct badges (badge)
kept_after_review.reason: Member-applied tags for browsing versus a curated editorial exhibit of extinct badges.

kept_after_review.pair: Badge search alias table (badge) vs Zero-result search to gap briefs (content)
kept_after_review.reason: The alias table is the search mechanism (synonyms that make a badge findable); the zero-result mining is the discovery process that suggests aliases. Related, not the same.

kept_after_review.pair: Badge knowledge profile (addon) vs Profile Guestbook (badge stamp) (content)
kept_after_review.reason: A knowledge score derived from play versus a guestbook of member stamps.

kept_after_review.pair: Rarity tier thresholds as chart reference rules (design) vs Contrast and colour-independence for rarity tiers and charts (design)
kept_after_review.reason: Reference lines marking tier boundaries on a chart versus a colour-blind-safe palette. Different mechanisms.

kept_after_review.pair: Encircle Territory Duel (game) vs Duels (game, on board)
kept_after_review.reason: The board's Duels is a challenge wrapper (best-of-three across the existing games); this is a new territory-capture board game played against a server AI. Only the word 'duel' overlaps.

kept_after_review.pair: Daily Badge Crossword (game) vs Silhouette, the daily badge guessing game (badge, on board)
kept_after_review.reason: A crossword over catalogue clues versus naming a silhouette. Different puzzle mechanics that happen to share a daily cadence.

kept_after_review.pair: Guest Showcase Slots (profile) vs Silent auction for one showcase slot a month (game, on board)
kept_after_review.reason: Letting a visitor hold a slot on someone else's profile versus auctioning one site-wide podium slot for coins.

kept_after_review.pair: Daily Catalog Solitaire (game) vs Daily Catalog Conditions (game)
kept_after_review.reason: A solitaire game versus daily modifiers applied to the arcade. The flag was purely the shared 'Daily Catalog' prefix.

kept_after_review.pair: Badge rename tracker (badge) vs Badge Re-issue Tracker (stats)
kept_after_review.reason: Tracking a provider rename (and keeping the old name findable) versus detecting a badge returning after expiry and comparing its second-life owner curve.
